long_biography.plain_text:
Beda Diethelm brought practical electronics experience to Phonak's development as an international hearing-aid manufacturer. He trained with a radio and television technician, then took charge of production and technical work at Bommer, a hearing-aid supplier.

During his operating career, Phonak developed powerful behind-the-ear aids for children with severe hearing loss, opening an important export market in the United States. Diethelm withdrew from day-to-day work in 1997 after completion of the group's new technology centre in Stäfa. He concentrated on his board responsibilities, with Peter Pfluger succeeding him as chief operating officer.
